title: Cohere Model Vault: Verifiable Confidential AI Inference
gist: Cohere details the architecture of Confidential Computing on Model Vault (public beta on NVIDIA H100 GPUs on Microsoft Azure): a confidential VM extended to the GPU, OHTTP payload encryption to an attested environment, and client-side remote attestation that refuses to send data if measurements fail policy. Cohere is explicit about what stays outside the boundary (side channels, availability, app-level bugs, metadata such as API credential and model ID) and plans to open-source the stack and add NVIDIA B200 support before GA.

themes.theme: Extending the confidential boundary to the GPU

insights.claim: For AI inference, a confidential CPU environment is insufficient because much model computation runs on accelerators; Cohere Model Vault uses NVIDIA GPU Confidential Computing to protect GPU memory and encrypt CPU-GPU traffic so the trust boundary spans the confidential VM and the accelerator.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: GPU-level confidential computing is becoming a prerequisite feature for selling AI inference to regulated enterprises, favoring NVIDIA hardware with this capability.
insights.quote: For AI inference, however, the boundary cannot end at the CPU.
insights.locator: From confidential hardware to confidential inference

insights.claim: In Cohere Model Vault, the OS, drivers, inference server and their memory run in a confidential VM, policy restricts it to approved software, and operators have no interactive path into the workload.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Removing operator access is the core selling point that lets enterprises send sensitive data to a vendor-managed model.

insights.claim: Microsoft Azure supplies the underlying confidential computing infrastructure, while Cohere builds managed model-serving, encrypted request, attestation and customer-verification layers on top so customers do not have to assemble these controls themselves.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Shows a Cohere-Azure-NVIDIA stack partnership where Cohere captures value as the integration and managed-service layer.
insights.locator: Microsoft Azure provides the underlying confidential

insights.claim: Cohere argues TLS alone is insufficient for confidential inference because it does not keep every intermediary out of the plaintext path, so Model Vault encrypts the request payload with Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) to a public key tied to the attested confidential environment, and only the gateway inside that environment can decrypt it.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Application-layer end-to-end encryption separates operating the service from seeing the data, a design other inference providers may need to match.
insights.quote: This creates an important separation between operating the service and accessing the contents of the request.

insights.claim: Model Vault customers keep using the existing API and request formats because OHTTP protection is implemented in the client and infrastructure layers, so applications do not need redesigned payloads.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Low integration friction lowers the adoption barrier for confidential inference in existing enterprise apps.
insights.locator: Applications continue to use the Model

themes.theme: Attestation as an active enforcement control

insights.claim: Cohere's design separates attestation evidence (what environment is actually running, as signed measurements of hardware, firmware, OS and application) from policy (whether the customer is willing to trust that environment), so customers need not rely on Cohere's own assertion of trustworthiness.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Verifiable trust rather than vendor promises is how AI vendors aim to win regulated workloads.
insights.quote: Evidence describes what is running.Policy determines whether that environment should be trusted.
insights.locator: Remote attestation: proving what will process the request

insights.claim: In Model Vault the client checks the destination against the approved policy before each protected request, and refuses to send the payload if a software measurement changed or the GPU is not in confidential mode; evidence is renewed frequently and re-verified on each refresh.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Turning attestation into a fail-closed gate is a concrete differentiator versus confidential computing used only as audit evidence.
insights.quote: This turns attestation from an audit artifact into an active security control.

insights.claim: Cohere says confidential computing does not eliminate trust: the hardware, firmware, measured software, reference measurements and attestation infrastructure stay in the trusted computing base, but trust becomes smaller, explicit and measurable.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Buyers still carry hardware and attestation-provider dependency risk; the residual trust sits mostly with chip vendors and cloud attestation services.
insights.quote: Confidential computing does not eliminate trust. It makes trust smaller, explicit, measurable, and verifiable.

insights.claim: Within its threat model, Confidential Computing on Model Vault keeps prompts, documents, responses and model execution unreadable to the host OS, hypervisor, infrastructure administrators, the cloud provider and Cohere operators.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Excluding the cloud provider and the model vendor themselves addresses a key objection of regulated enterprises to hosted LLMs.

insights.claim: Cohere acknowledges Model Vault does not protect against some physical and side-channel attacks, denial of service, application-level vulnerabilities such as prompt injection or insecure tool use, or observable metadata such as request timing, message size, traffic volume, routing, the API credential and the model identifier.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Confidential inference does not replace AI application security, so separate demand for agent and app-layer security tools remains.
insights.locator: What remains outside the protection boundary

insights.claim: Cohere states confidential computing is not a data-residency mechanism, not a replacement for compliance or contractual controls such as DPAs, and not homomorphic encryption, since the model still runs on plaintext inside the protected environment.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Sovereignty and residency requirements still need separate in-region deployments; confidential computing does not displace sovereign-cloud demand.

insights.claim: Confidential Computing on Model Vault builds on Kata Containers and Confidential Containers, and Cohere intends to open-source its confidential inference stack so customers can inspect the code and reproduce attestation measurements.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing the stack could make it a reference design for confidential inference and pressure competitors on transparency; watch for the release.
insights.quote: attestation should not require customers to accept another black box.

insights.claim: Cohere's confidential Model Vault public beta runs on NVIDIA H100 GPUs on Microsoft Azure, and Cohere is working toward NVIDIA Blackwell support, including B200 GPUs, on the way to general availability.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: GA timing is tied to confidential-mode Blackwell capacity on Azure; a milestone to track for Cohere's enterprise push.
